items.note: The page states the identity $QF_{\boldsymbol t}u=\overline a\cdot\frac{a*(\overline a\cdot u)}{T}$ under the hypothesis that every $t_i$ is even, with $F_{\boldsymbol t}$ normalized by $1/T$ and using the negative sign, and $Q$ reading frequency $(-s_ij_i)_i$, all as in the paper (lines 3506-3511, 3557, 3911-3925). It then proves it the way the paper's proof does: periodicity, then the coefficient of $u_{\boldsymbol k}$, then matching that coefficient with $QF_{\boldsymbol t}$.

The page defines the chirp exactly as the paper does: "Define the chirp $a_{\boldsymbol j}=\exp\left(-\pi i\sum_{i=1}^d s_ij_i^2/t_i\right)$". It also explains why the factor $s_i$ in the chirp encodes $Q$.

The page computes the change explicitly, "$-\pi i s_i\frac{(j_i+t_i)^2-j_i^2}{t_i}=-\pi i s_i(2j_i+t_i)$, which is an integral multiple of $2\pi i$ because $t_i$ is even". This is correct and matches the paper. It also explains why periodicity is needed: the cyclic convolution reads $a$ modulo $t_i$.

The page writes the coefficient as $\frac1T\overline a_{\boldsymbol j}a_{\boldsymbol j-\boldsymbol k}\overline a_{\boldsymbol k}$, expands $(j_i-k_i)^2$, and gives the combined exponent $\sum_i\frac{\pi i s_i}{t_i}(j_i^2-(j_i^2-2j_ik_i+k_i^2)+k_i^2)$, which simplifies to $2\pi i\sum_is_ij_ik_i/t_i$. The algebra and the signs are correct, and the result matches the paper's display (lines 3943-3949).

The Setting gives $(F_{\boldsymbol t}u)_{\boldsymbol f}$ with the explicit negative-sign kernel and says $Q$ puts at position $\boldsymbol j$ the entry of frequency $(-s_ij_i)_i$, which matches $(P_tv)_k=v_{-sk}$ in the paper. Substituting gives the stated coefficient $\frac1T\exp(2\pi i\sum_is_ij_ik_i/t_i)$. The page then matches the two coefficients, as the paper does.

errors.quote: The permuted transform is thus reduced to one [Cyclic convolution](convolution.md) of length $T$ between two pointwise phase multiplications.
errors.problem: The convolution is a $d$-dimensional cyclic convolution on $\prod_i\mathbb Z/t_i\mathbb Z$ with $T$ entries. The paper calls it "cyclic convolution on the product of the coordinate groups" (lines 3907-3909). Because every $t_i$ is even, this group is not $\mathbb Z/T\mathbb Z$ when $d\ge2$, so "of length $T$" wrongly suggests a one-dimensional length-$T$ convolution. The page's own derivation correctly reduces indices coordinatewise, modulo $t_i$.

errors.quote: Executing $Q$ means sorting data on tapes, which costs a logarithmic factor beyond a linear pass, the kind of factor the power saving removes.
errors.problem: The power saving removes only a factor $(\lg n)^{\kappa}$ with $\kappa=2^{-182}$, not a logarithmic factor. The real point is that a label-and-sort, which costs $O(tp\log t)$ against a linear $O(tp)$ (paper lines 3692-3693), would add a full logarithmic overhead that the much smaller saving cannot absorb.
